OMG, thank you to whoever did this! Thanks to the archive! I worked at an official Hitachi service center in the 90s. One day, Hitachi told us we couldn't buy proprietary parts and then came repair manuals. We could pay a $300 to factory refurb or tell the customer to buy new. Tweet by @textfiles

https://x.com/textfiles/status/1291959856098881536

1291968177434501121.a: A new 19" TV cost $150 at the time and it cost $300 to repair it after this policy change. Also, the reason they switched to proprietary parts is that they would install a 3amp transistor in a 3amp circuit. It died days out of warranty. We replaced with a 5amp so it never failed.

1291969197099057152.a: Electronic parts are rated for a certain number of hours at a particular temperature at full power. So if you use a 3amp and run it full blast it will last like 10,000 hrs or 416 days of continuous operation. 8 hrs/day is 3 years. But a 5A runs cold at 3A and never deteriorates.
